collection_metadata.collection_method: open-source web search aggregation (search snippets only)
limitations: Direct page fetches (ncsc.gov.uk, bleepingcomputer.com and others) failed in this environment; content is drawn from search-result summaries and may be inaccurate. Verify against primary sources.
Search surfaced little dated within the last 24 hours; several results had unreliable date metadata. No UK government incident confirmed in the window.
Attribution statements (ShinyHunters, Russian-speaking actors) are press reports, not confirmed.
KQL queries are untested hunting starting points; validate table availability and tune before use.
Citrix indicator values are relayed from secondary sources; use vendor IoC tooling for full lists.

confidence_legend.high: Corroborated by the vendor advisory or by multiple independent reputable sources.
confidence_legend.medium: Reported by a single reputable source, or by secondary coverage of a primary source not directly accessible.
confidence_legend.low: Single-sourced and uncorroborated; treat as an investigative lead only.

vulnerabilities.title: Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation - NCSC and NHS England Alerts; UK Follow-on SAML Flaw Pending (CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772, CVE-2026-107406)
affected_products: Hybrid Secure Private Access deployments using NetScaler
vulnerabilities.summary: The UK NCSC has told UK organisations to mitigate Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaws promptly after confirming reports of active exploitation of CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution, CVSS 9.5, affects default configurations) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow leading to code execution or DoS, CVSS 9.5, requires DTLS, which is on by default for VPN virtual servers). Citrix disclosed them on 2026-09-27 (bulletin CTX697096) and CISA added both to KEV the same day with a 2026-09-30 federal deadline, but researchers report webshell deployment since early September, i.e. exploitation preceded disclosure. NHS England's National CSOC issued alert CC-4858 (2026-09-28) rating further exploitation 'almost certain', and a follow-on alert CC-4865 (updated 2026-10-09) covers a separate critical SAML memory-overflow flaw, CVE-2026-107406, which NHS CSOC assesses as likely to be exploited but which is not reported exploited. NetScaler is common in UK central government, NHS trusts, councils and corporate remote-access estates; no UK-specific exposure count was found (global counts range from ~21,000 to ~50,000 exposed instances depending on scanner). Post-exploitation reporting describes web shells (WHIPSHOT), a Python tunneller (SLAPSHOT) and a custom remote-management implant (Platypus) with a replaced customsnmpd. Patching alone does not evict an implant: appliances exposed since early September should be treated as potentially compromised. NOTE: this item is a carry-over/escalation from late September rather than a first report inside the 24h window; it is included because it is the only confirmed, actively exploited issue with direct NCSC and NHS England UK advisories and a pending follow-on CVE. Indicator detail comes from secondary vendor blogs - verify against Citrix's IoC scanner and the NCSC page. Primary pages could not be fetched directly in this run.
recommended_actions: Upgrade to 14.1-73.37 / 13.1-64.23 or later and then apply the fix for CVE-2026-107406 as it lands; do not rely on mitigation alone.
Run Citrix's IoC checker and review appliances for the listed file paths, unexpected .deb files and replaced customsnmpd; treat hits as full compromise.
Rotate credentials and secrets stored on or reachable from the appliance, and invalidate VPN sessions.
Restrict management and gateway exposure; forward NetScaler logs to Sentinel.
Follow NCSC and NHS England Digital cyber alerts CC-4858/CC-4865 for updates.

kql.name: Citrix NetScaler - exploitation artefact file paths
kql.description: Applies if NetScaler/Linux telemetry or file-integrity logs reach MDE. Otherwise port to FIM or syslog.
kql.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(45d)
| where FolderPath has_any ("/vpn/scripts/linux/","/var/netscaler/logon/LogonPoint/custom/")
| where FileName in~ ("nsgclient18.deb","nsg64.deb",".ctxs.receiver") or FileName endswith ".deb"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc

kql.name: Citrix NetScaler - post-patch outbound connections from appliances
kql.description: Populate ns_ips. Flags appliance-originated outbound connections to non-allow-listed public destinations (implant C2 / tunnelling).
kql.query:
let ns_ips = dynamic(["<NETSCALER_SNIP_OR_NSIP>"]);
let allowed = dynamic(["<NTP/DNS/UPDATE_IPs>"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
| where SourceIP in (ns_ips)
| where DestinationIP !in (allowed) and not(ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP))
| summarize Connections=count(), Ports=make_set(DestinationPort,20), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by SourceIP, DestinationIP
| sort by Connections desc

kql.name: Citrix NetScaler - suspicious activity in appliance syslog
kql.description: Looks for shell/webshell keywords in NetScaler syslog. Field names vary by build; tune.
kql.query:
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
| where Computer has_any ("netscaler","ns") or ProcessName has "nsppe"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("WHIPSHOT","SLAPSHOT","customsnmpd",".ctxs.receiver","nsgclient18","/bin/sh -c")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

iocs.context: Hidden artefact in LogonPoint custom directory.
Custom remote-management implant delivered after exploitation; replaced customsnmpd.

iocs.value: Full IP/hash lists (58 attacker IPs, webshell SHA-256) exist in Citrix IoC checker v1.4 / vendor reports and were not transcribed.

vulnerabilities.title: TFG London (Hobbs, Whistles, Phase Eight) Cyber Incident Disrupts UK Retail IT Systems; Second UK Retailer Incident in a Week
affected_products: TFG London corporate IT and e-commerce systems supporting Phase Eight, Hobbs and Whistles
vulnerabilities.summary: TFG London, the UK arm of South Africa's Foschini Group, disclosed on 2026-10-13 that it detected a cyber incident on Sunday 2026-10-11 affecting IT systems for the Phase Eight, Hobbs and Whistles brands. Stores remain open but several systems are down, some websites are impaired and online orders placed since 2026-10-11 may be delayed; customers have been asked not to resubmit orders. The company has engaged external specialists, activated incident-response and continuity plans, notified UK authorities and says it has no reason to believe payment details are at risk, but has not yet determined whether customer or other data was taken. Inside Story and White Stuff run on separate systems and were not affected. Press describes it as the second attack on a UK retailer in about a week (ASOS disclosed unauthorised access to personal data the previous week). Some outlets link the activity to the ShinyHunters group; TFG has not confirmed attribution, so treat that as an unverified lead. No CVE, initial access vector or IOCs have been published. Relevance to UK corporates: continued targeting of UK retail via help-desk social engineering, third-party and SaaS access has been the pattern since the 2025 M&S/Co-op/Harrods wave.
recommended_actions: Retail and consumer brands: review help-desk identity-verification and MFA reset procedures and privileged-access paths.
Monitor for phishing/smishing impersonating the affected brands; customers should not resubmit orders or follow links in unsolicited messages.
Review third-party/SaaS (CRM, ticketing, data-warehouse) tokens and OAuth grants for anomalous access.
Watch ICO and TFG statements for confirmation of data impact.

kql.name: Help-desk driven MFA/password resets followed by risky sign-in
kql.description: Generic hunt for the social-engineering pattern used against UK retailers. Not specific to TFG; no IOCs published.
kql.query:
let resets = AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where OperationName in ("Reset password (by admin)","Reset user password","User registered security info","Admin registered security info")
| extend Target = tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName)
| project ResetTime=TimeGenerated, Target, OperationName, Actor=tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName);
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) and RiskLevelDuringSignIn in ("medium","high")
| join kind=inner resets on $left.UserPrincipalName == $right.Target
| where TimeGenerated between (ResetTime .. ResetTime + 4h)
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, AppDisplayName, OperationName, Actor, RiskLevelDuringSignIn

iocs.context: Some media link the incident to this group; TFG has not confirmed.

iocs.value: No technical indicators have been published for the TFG London incident.

vulnerabilities.title: ASOS Customer Data Exposure - Unauthorised Access to Personal Data and Account Takeover (Credential Stuffing Reported)
vulnerabilities.summary: Press on 2026-10-13 cites ASOS having said an 'unauthorised party' accessed some personal data (names and contact details) the week before the TFG London incident. Separately, US breach notifications dated 2026-08-21 describe an ASOS account-takeover incident (unusual activity found 2026-07-28, unauthorised access confirmed 2026-07-29; ~138,828 individuals; credential stuffing consistent). It is not established that these are the same event, and no ASOS primary statement was retrieved in this run, so scope and vector for the October disclosure are unverified. Included for UK corporate relevance and because retailers are being targeted in sequence.
recommended_actions: Enforce MFA/passkeys and credential-stuffing controls (rate limiting, bot management, breached-password screening) on customer login.
Advise customers to use unique passwords and watch for phishing referencing the brand.
Confirm scope with ASOS/ICO statements before treating as a single event.

kql.name: Credential stuffing - many distinct usernames from one IP on login endpoint
kql.description: Generic detection for customer-facing login abuse; adjust the URI to your login path.
kql.query:
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod == "POST" and csUriStem has_any ("/login","/signin","/account/authenticate")
| summarize Attempts=count(), Failures=countif(scStatus in (401,403)), Users=dcount(csUserName) by cIP, bin(TimeGenerated,15m)
| where Attempts > 50 and Users > 20
| sort by Attempts desc

iocs.value: Credential stuffing / account takeover using reused credentials
iocs.context: Reported vector for the August 2026 ASOS notification; ATT&CK T1110.004.

vulnerabilities.title: Carry-over: 'FortiBleed' - Stolen Fortinet Firewall Credentials Include UK Government, Embassy, Council and NHS Accounts Offered for Sale
affected_products: Fortinet FortiGate appliances (reported ~70,000-86,000 devices / credential sets, 194 countries)
vulnerabilities.summary: Telegraph-led reporting from July 2026 says Russian-speaking actors harvested credentials from tens of thousands of Fortinet firewalls ('FortiBleed'); leaked/for-sale lists reportedly include IT staff at UK embassies (Thailand, Mauritius), local-authority staff (Derbyshire, Waltham Forest), and NHS, energy and medicine-supplier logins, with access priced up to ~$60,000. Counts vary by source (SOCRadar: 86,644 credentials). No formal state attribution and no NCSC/Fortinet PSIRT/CISA confirmation was found. This is NOT new in the 24h window - no fresh development was found - and is carried only because it is the most UK-government-specific credential exposure identified. Confidence is low; treat as a lead for credential rotation and exposure review.
recommended_actions: Rotate all credentials and secrets on FortiGate devices and any accounts authenticating through them; invalidate VPN sessions.
Patch FortiOS to the latest release and review for unknown admin accounts, config changes and exposed management interfaces.
Check dark-web/credential-leak monitoring for your domains.

kql.name: Fortinet - new admin accounts or config changes
kql.description: Detects admin/user creation and configuration changes in FortiGate CEF logs.
kql.query:
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where Activity has_any ("Add admin","Add user","Edit admin","Configuration changed","Attribute configured") or AdditionalExtensions has "cfgpath"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SourceIP, SourceUserName, Activity, Message
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

iocs.context: Per press reporting; no formal attribution.

iocs.value: No technical indicators identified for FortiBleed in this run.

ttp.value: Credential stuffing / account takeover using reused credentials

summary_statistics.highest_priority_action: Patch Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2026-88771/88772, NCSC and NHS England alerted) and hunt for implants on appliances exposed since early September; track TFG London (Hobbs/Whistles/Phase Eight) incident for data-impact confirmation.
